title: Maximum-Area Rectangle Inscribed in a Circle
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Among all rectangles inscribed in a circle of radius 1, find the dimensions that maximize the area and compute that maximum area.

steps.title: Translate Inscribing into a Constraint
steps.explanation: The diagonal of an inscribed rectangle is a diameter of the circle, so the Pythagorean theorem links width w and height h to the diameter 2.
steps.why: A rectangle is cyclic with its center at the circle's center; the diagonal must therefore span the full diameter 2r = 2.

steps.title: Square the Objective
steps.explanation: Maximizing positive A is equivalent to maximizing A^2, which is a product of the squared sides u = w^2 and v = h^2 subject to u + v = 4.
steps.why: Squaring is an increasing map on positive areas, so it preserves the location of the maximum while linearizing the constraint.

steps.title: Apply the Fixed-Sum Product Principle
steps.explanation: For a fixed sum, the product uv is largest when u = v = 2 (AM-GM, or completing the square on u(4-u)); this caps the area at 2.
steps.why: The parabola u(4 - u) opens downward with vertex at u = 2, so the equal-split configuration is the unique maximizer.

steps.title: Recover the Dimensions and Verify Attainability
steps.explanation: Both squared sides equal 2, giving the square of side sqrt(2); it satisfies the diagonal constraint and attains area sqrt(2) * sqrt(2) = 2, so the bound is sharp.
steps.why: An upper bound proven from the constraint and achieved by a concrete feasible rectangle is by definition the maximum.
